utterances.text: And after you'd been arrested and whilst your wife was still in Sanski Most with your children, did anything happen to your house? You've told us how the police searched your house and took your ID. But did anything happen to your house?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They destroyed the roof with zoljas. They fired through the wall. My son was upstairs, and a zolja went through the -- through the wall, under the bed. Luckily he didn't die. The house was completely affected, damaged. They fired in front of the house. It was set on fire. But a Serb, a boy, from the neighbourhood and a Muslim, they went in and put the fire out. And I've been repairing that now. I've been repairing the house. That's what happened. My wife had serious problems while she was in Sanski Most and she then left via Zagreb and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, doctor.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner. Who's going to go first? Yes. Dr. Sabanovic, you are now going to be cross-examined by the Defence team, by lead counsel, I suppose, for Radoslav Brdjanin, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Ackerman, wherever you like. If you want to change place, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The problem is, Your Honour, they have rearranged this courtroom to accommodate Mr. Milosevic and it doesn't work for the rest of us any more. So I'm going to try to move this thing here and see what happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. You're free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Maybe it will work; maybe it won't. I think it will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If there are any jugs full of water, please keep them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That works pretty good. All right. I'm ready, Your Honour. With your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My name is John Ackerman. I'm counsel for Mr. Brdjanin. And I've got a few questions I want to ask you. I think the Judge would agree with me that probably the easiest way for you and I to get through this is for you to listen very carefully to the questions I ask you. And if it's possible for you to answer them with a "yes" or "no," you could do that. Is that okay with you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm going to talk about some of the things that you've just finished talking about this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I'm going to need someone's help or indulgence or something, because based upon some testimony that I heard this afternoon, I need a document that I don't have, and it is that pen and ink drawing of Manjaca. And I don't know -- I don't know what its exhibit number is or anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's included in one of these -- included in one of the statements that the witness made in -- to the authorities in Germany. However, the copy that I have is for reasons I don't understand divided into two pages. That's -- but I'm sure, Ms. Korner, that Ms. Gustin can help us identify -- this is the drawing, the sketch of the Manjaca camp. I don't --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I was hoping the registry might be able to provide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It is an exhibit, but I don't know what exhibit number, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. P467.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: While we are finding that document, sir, you saw a videotape a while ago of some prisoners in Manjaca. And one of those prisoners we stopped and looked at for a moment, and he was described by you as being nothing but skin and bones. That was one of the prisoners that came from Omarska; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And was that person ever examined by you? Did you ever examine him to find out if he had any particular medical problems?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us the result of your examination of him.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the result of the examination was the diagnosis of what we call cohexia [phoen]. He had been undernourished. The conditions he lived in were terrible. The living conditions were terrible. It was a result of force used against him, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Pardon me, Mr. Ackerman. Ms. Korner, the document that you referred us to is signed by one of the previous witnesses, and it has some numbers. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's not problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's nothing problematic according me. But do you have any --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Ms. Gustin pointed out that it had been marked by Medic. But I think Mr. Ackerman just wants to orientate himself. That's all, so I don't think it matters at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: She's right. We've discussed this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: She probably knows more about what I am doing than I do. It's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you want the document placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. I want it brought to me. So I can look at it. And then when I get around to it, I'm going to use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. I'd like the three photographs, 808, 809, and 810 to be made available to the witness. 808 is not important. 809 and 810 are the ones I really want to look at. Let's look at 809 first, please. Can you put that on the ELMO first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you look at 809 -- you can't see it on the ELMO, because you can't see it all. But over on the far right of that picture you will see an iron gate. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in fact, there is an entrance to the Manjaca camp where that gate is.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And to the right, there's an -- there's the administration building. And I think the barracks that some of the camp personnel stayed in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up in the left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah. And just as a kind of orientation, if we looked a little bit further to the left on this picture, we'd see the guard tower, wouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And basically we're looking in generally a south direction as we look at this photograph. Toward the south.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the other witness's microphone be switched on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the other thing I'd like you to notice, just looking at this photograph, you see the two persons behind the water tank, the ones that seem to be moving the two together between the water tank and the flag pole?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left, next to the water tanker?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, they're just -- the two people that are in the open behind the water tank are the two people I'm trying to refer you to. Do you see them?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The thing I want you to notice is that it's -- it's apparently close to midday because there are hardly any shadows in this photograph. The shadows are -- well, there are some, but not elongated. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, looks like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now what I'd like to do is look at 810. And I want the usher to also hand you P467. And this gate that we see in 810, can you tell us where that gate is on the drawing P467?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, the Chamber needs to follow this, and the document P467 ought to be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we are to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as he finds where it is, we'll put it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, can you show us then now, sir, on the ELMO where the gate we see in the photograph is, located?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is up there. But it doesn't really mean anything to me. I'm no architect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dr. Sabanovic, you have to show us on the document itself on the paper that you have in front of you. So for the record, Mr. Ackerman, the Chamber notes that the witness has indicated the spot behind -- immediately behind shed numbered 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in front of the shed that is immediately behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that, sir, is the -- the other part of Manjaca, the sort of camp number 2 or whatever you might call it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That side, over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. And now look at 810 again, will you please. Now, what were you doing over on that side?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the camp. I'm coming out waiting for this one to let me through to get to the infirmary, to let me through. This is the main entrance into the camp. I am inside, and he is on the same side. He will open it, and I will go down to the command where the infirmary is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So were you -- were you housed over on that side of the camp?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's this side of the camp. It's the third stable. That's what it was called. The first one is at the entrance next to the gate. And the last one is that one down there. One, two, three.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So did you move over there after you first went to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I moved where? I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: To the -- that other part of the camp, the second half of the camp, the part that you're standing in in this photograph. It's my understanding -- let me just -- I'm confusing both you and myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. I think you can rephrase the whole series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By asking him first when he arrived in Manjaca where he was put.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Please put the drawing back on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And whether he remained there --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Show me which of these barns was the one that you were housed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When he first arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When you first arrived at Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you're pointing at the back row of barns and what would be the barn behind what is marked number 1 on this exhibit, P467; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the third stable in a row. Come, I was there for several months, the first to come, the first to leave. Skip those formalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And show me where the command is, where the offices are. Point to those on this diagram.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an architect. Sorry. Where were they? The offices, where they were. That is where they were. And I went past them a million times. I cannot show you whether these are offices or what. I can't really get my bearings in sketches and drawings and such like. The offices are as you come out through the main gate, you turn right, just a little bit to the right, and a bit down, and then you go there. That is where the offices were. To the gentlemen where in the Manjaca camp, it's no secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You see the guard tower in this drawing, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I -- I see nothing on this drawing. Oh, sure. Yes, of course I see it. How could I not see it. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You know where the guard tower was in relationship to the offices and the barracks, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above -- above the entrance to the camp where you come out of the camp to the right. Here it is. That is where it is. That is the observation tower where the policemen usually are. And below it -- now, down here are offices, or as you call it, the command, or offices. Formalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are getting there, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, look at 809 again, please, the photograph. Now, we've looked at this before. You've described that iron gate as the main gate and that building there as the command. And if you are standing at that gate facing up that road toward the south, that's where the guard tower is; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, you were there for months. You probably know more about that than me. Is that where it was or not? Do you have an answer?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What answer? These are formalities. I know where every hole is, and now you ask me about some drawings or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm not asking you --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is simply unnecessary and --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm going to ask you about a lot of drawings and you're going to answer my questions and you're not going to tell me I'm asking you formalities. I have a right to ask questions and you have to answer them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Let me handle this. Dr. Sabanovic, look at me. I know that coming here and giving evidence for you is no fun. I have no doubt about that. But it's no fun either for the Defence counsel to defend his client. The Defence counsel has a duty to defend his client, and he has a duty to cross-examine you, and I have a duty to allow him to cross-examine you by putting questions that he has a right to put. But if he has a right to put those questions to you, you have a duty to answer them. I will not allow you to enter into a collision path with the Defence counsel who is going to -- who is doing his duty here. I will be the one to stop him when he puts a question to you which I think and the other Judges agree with me that shouldn't be put or that you shouldn't answer. But until I stop Mr. Ackerman, please do answer his questions. It's not a formality. He may have his reasons. We will soon know what his reasons are. But in the meantime, please do not make our life more difficult than it already is and do try to answer his questions. Thank you. Mr. Ackerman, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I want you to look again now at photograph P810, the one that you are in. Do you recall what was happening when that photograph was taken? Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You told us when Ms. Korner was asking you questions that it was toward the end of your confinement there, because you looked pretty good in that photograph. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you left there in November?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dr. Sabanovic, the question was: Did you leave there in November? What did you answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm asking you because the interpreters didn't hear you. They didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And sir, won't you agree with me from the looks of the grass and the trees that this picture was taken in the summertime?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. It must have been July or August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. And July would have been shortly after the first visit of the ICRC; right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, if this gate is where you showed us on the diagram that it is, you are facing south as you stand there, are you not?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And because the sun is shining on your left side, I guess we can conclude -- and the shadow is very long -- that it's very early morning in the summertime.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, around 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, you've also told us that you were -- you were in the same -- well, let me ask you. Let me make sure that we're correct about this. You were in the same building, the same stable, as Dr. Derviskadic?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that was that one behind number 1 that you showed us in the diagram; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let's put the diagram of the stables back up there again.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last one from the entrance here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd really like to mark it, but I don't have permission -- unless I get permission from the Prosecutor, I can't. Because it's her exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. If it's necessary, we can get a clean version from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I mean, if it really is necessary. It means we'll have to go and get one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We can do it at the next break, I hope, because I really -- I really would like to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And if I can find one, I'll use my own. But I don't think I've got one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can provide one after the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner. In the meantime, looking at the ELMO and looking at the document again, perhaps Dr. Sabanovic can once more indicate to us the shed where he was lodged when he arrived in Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, he's now pointing in a different one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm wondering if this exercise is going to get anybody --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't want to stop from Mr. Ackerman at this point in time because I don't know where he's getting --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If it's really necessary. Because it seems to me it's going to end up in the most appalling condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, it's actually getting a lot more interesting, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, you showed us now that you were in a barn that has a number "1" written on it in red; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And show us again the gate that you say is the one shown in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now it's the one in the front by the guard tower; correct? That's the one you say it is?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If the witness could now be handed P807.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ackerman. For the record, the Chamber notes that upon being asked to indicate the barn where he was lodged, the witness indicated the barn which in the original document P467 is already marked by a previous witness with a number "1" written in red. Upon being asked to indicate the gate to which a previous question was addressed, the witness now indicates the gate that is immediately visible in front of the barn on the same document which is marked with the number "3" written in red. Yes. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Please put P807 now on the ELMO. And focus in and enlarge as much as possible photograph number 2. Now, stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, it says that that photograph number 2 there is a view from the stables from the tower. So if the fence were still there, I guess we would see right there on that road the gate that you have just referred to, and those would be the stables in which you say one of which you were confined.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't really understand all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if you compare that photograph number 2 with P810. P810 has a building that shouldn't be there and is missing a bunch of trees that should be there, isn't it? So that can't be the same view, can it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the main gate. This wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's about as clear as it's going to get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Ackerman, if my recollection of previous witnesses is correct, it seems to me that the probability is that there was first gate that came before where the command or the first group of buildings was, and then there is another gate which is specific to the barns. That's my recollection. But I may be -- I may be wrong. But perhaps if that is taken into consideration by you and also by the witness, maybe I'm not far off the mark. If I remember well, before you even reach the command post and where the command buildings were, there was a gate there, and that's the first stop. Then once you are in, separating the area where the command was and the area where the barns were, there was another gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's really very simple. If you look at photographs 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But those -- those are recent photographs, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand they're recent. But the buildings are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, the buildings --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the trees are the same. And if you look at 2 and 3, you will see that copse of trees on the left-hand side. You can't miss it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it goes past those three stables. If you look at P810, where those trees are there is a building. And it's clearly one of the old buildings. And what he said initially, that this is the back part of Manjaca was correct, that's what it is. It's that second gate that he initially pointed out. It can't be anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will not argue with you on that. I don't know. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I think we can clear it up later on. But we're not going to be able to do it with this witness. That's pretty clear with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. But if there's a point Mr. Ackerman -- Mr. Inayat is very familiar with the layout and he can do the whole thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To me -- I think that would be useful. But on the other hand, hearing what -- hearing what you have just stated. If the sketch, the diagram that we've seen, is correct, then one would expect the buildings on the left-hand side of this photograph to be parallel with the buildings on the right-hand side. And that building on the left side is definitely not parallel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think somebody --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not -- I don't know. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Somebody said, Your Honour, it's not a very good sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah. I've taken a position from the beginning that that sketch is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that's right. I don't think it's an accurate sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's got the wrong entrance and it's missing the command building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, you're free to bring whatever evidence you require, Mr. Ackerman, and Ms. Korner to clear this up if it is important, which I suppose it is. But don't put too much pressure on the witness, who I understand is not exactly the ideal person to enlighten us on -- on sketches, diagram, maps, and all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm finished with it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm going elsewhere. What time do you break? 5.15 or 5.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 5.15. Unless you require a break earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that you were describing a little while ago the latrines that were dug between the two buildings and the oak timbers that were put on those latrine. And you said that when the Red Cross came to visit, representatives from the Red Cross fainted. Now, did you treat them after they had fainted in any way? Did you give them medical attention after they had fainted? The Red Cross representatives who fainted, did you give them medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Collapse is something when a man needs to lie down for five minutes just to be horizontal, and after that he can sit up. This is not a physical injury or something. It is a mental state where one cannot bear the sight of something and one simply falls down, spends five minutes on the ground, and five minutes later he can sit and stand up. I mean, they are healthy people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah. How many of them fainted? How many of the Red Cross representatives fainted there?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you. Two, three, or one. It doesn't matter. At any rate, I mean, when they saw it, I mean, it's always two or three of them who come, not more than that. And they were mostly women.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, it matters to me because you said they fainted, and you apparently saw that happen. How many of them fainted?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So tell us how many.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Three fainted. All three of them?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three women. We were several. We didn't all faint. Unconsciousness, collapse. Every literate man knows what a collapse is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going back now to the beginning of your testimony yesterday. After the war started in Croatia, you told us yesterday that you started issuing false medical certificates to young men to assist them in avoiding mobilisation and going off to fight in Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Issue the certificate. I did issue medical certificates. And my colleague, who's called Knezevic, doctor, general medicine, a Serb, he went to Jasenovac and he died in the Jasenovac camp. He was brought to Sanski Most. You can look for it and you'll find it. Not false. I issued medical certificates to people so they wouldn't have to go to war. I'm an opponent of war. That is not my -- that is not in my -- that is my country, and it cannot be my objective to see people get killed for no purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, in those medical certificates, you described medical conditions that these people did not have, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You described them as being unfit for military service, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That was not a true, was it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But they were fit for military service, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Physically fit. They were physically fit, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You issued certificates to as many as 2.000 people. You helped them not go to war because you thought they shouldn't go to war. Right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for them to go. They are not fit. They should not go. They should not lose their lives, just as Dr. Knezevic, who died without the need to fight in Croatia and Serbia, and he lived nicely in his own country and then he lost his life because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: At page 12 of the LiveNote transcript, the Prosecutor asked you this question: "In other words, are you saying some of the people to whom you issued medical certificates in fact were fit to go?" Answer: "Yes. There were those who were able-bodied. And let me also tell you, there were equally Serbs, Croats, and Muslims amongst them. There were even Serbs." And then you talked about your belief against --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There are documents which you wrote and signed saying that these people were not fit, were not true. They are lies.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not lies. Don't use such jargon when speaking to me. I won't allow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When someone is not fit and you certify that they are fit, that is not the truth; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is one thing and a lie is another thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Answer my question. They were not the truth, were they?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You believed and do believe now that you were serving a greater good by helping them avoid becoming involved in what you believed was an unjust war; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You felt justified in being untruthful regarding the issuance of these certificates because of your feelings about the war.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not completely. Not completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You felt justified, because you continued to do it even after you were warned, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The medical doctrine -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to talk about your arrest now. You gave several -- I shouldn't say several. You've given a couple of statements, one fairly long, over several days to authorities in Germany. And that was basically in May of 1999. And then you gave another statement to the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor in 1/2 December 2000 and 14/17/19 February 2001. I'm going to be asking you questions from both of those statements. And in fairness to you, I would like you to have them in front of you, so I'll ask the Prosecutor to give them to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I don't know if you are aware of this, but we have of course the statement that the witness gave or released in May of 1999 to the German authorities, and none of us seems to have the other two statements that Mr. Ackerman has just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] No. He's not -- I'm sorry. I keep forgetting to turn my microphone on this court. Your Honour, the statement, the ICTY statement is actually taken over a period of December and February. There's only two. German and the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But that -- the ICTY one we don't have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You do have it. That's what I've been referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have that. We have the German one. None of us have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I do not understand how that happened, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It can be solved. I mean, it's -- I'm just pointing this out, because obviously if there are questions forthcoming from Mr. Ackerman based on those two -- on that statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very sorry, but I -- and I have every faith in Ms. Gustin infallibility on this one. The statements were handed to the Court on the 31st of May, ICTY. And I don't know how they didn't get to Your Honour, but I think Your Honour will have to make inquiries. But we can get some more copies. Then Your Honour must have been quite surprised by the number of questions I've been asking which have no basis whatsoever either in the proofing document or in the German statements. If Your Honours don't get the statement in advance, perhaps Your Honours would be kind enough to let us know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. No. But we didn't know about the existence of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can tell Your Honour that all the witnesses we're calling without exception have some kind of a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We did have -- we did have a note which -- in English which said Witness 7.100 during proofing on the 1st of June, plus bulleted points.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that was not accompanied --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It wasn't, because the statement was handed out in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But this is what we got on, I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You got that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We got this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The actual statement of the witness though was handed out on the -- whatever date it was, the 31st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Anyway, I think Your Honour the only way that we can deal with this. If Your Honour feel that is you're -- I can always check that you've got the statements with us. But I think this really you'll have to bring it up with Your Honours' staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, please, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm at your pleasure, Your Honour. If you want to take a few moments now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. I'll go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll be able to follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I want to talk to you about your arrest in Sanski Most. If you look at the first page of the statement that you made to the German authorities. I think it's page 2. And I'll look at the B/C/S. Yes, it's page 2, halfway down, begins [B/C/S spoken] 26. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not important. Just ask me the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It says: "I was seized by uniformed Chetniks in the health centre at about 2100 hours on 26 May 1992." And in terms of your statement to the German authorities, that's what you told them about your arrest, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that yesterday and very well. This is a translation mistake. But when I got to the hospital where I was called, I said that I had been arrested, the police and the hospital took me home, escorted me home, and then I was taken to the Crisis Staff. I don't know. This is simply not comprehensible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir. I know what you said yesterday. I'm asking you if it's correct that this is what you told the German police. If it's not what you'll told the German police, just say so.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that -- what I said yesterday, and what I said to the German authorities I couldn't have said that. The translation wasn't correct. That's probably the reason. The person who translated this probably didn't do so correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor on the dates that we've talked about, on page 4, I believe it is, you told the representatives of the Prosecutor that you were arrested on 26 May 1992 at 1800, three hours earlier than what you -- apparently the German statement indicates -- while you were at home. That's what you told the Prosecutor; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th of May. On the 26th of May, both the Germans and in this place. On the 26th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. But the statement you made to the Prosecutor, page 4: "I was arrested on the 26th May 1992 at 1800 while I was home." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So they got it wrong too?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Were you listening yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you questions today. And you'll answer them. The Judge will instruct you to answer it.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm answering them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: According to your statement to the Prosecutor, what you told the Prosecutor's investigators was that you were arrested 26 May 1992 at 1800 while you were home. Now, did -- was that -- did you say that or not?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 2000 hours and 2100 hours. That's what I told the Prosecution. That's what it was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So they got it wrong.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the -- from the health centre home and then to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So the German authorities failed to write down what you said properly; the Prosecutor failed to write down what you said properly. Let's see if you agree that the court reporter here in court got it right yesterday. Page 19 of your testimony, the court reporter here in court says that you got a call. You were at home. You got a call from Bosko Grubisa at around 8.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There was a very severe patient and that I should go there because he needed to consult me. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's the true one; right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And when you said 8.00, I assume you meant 8.00 in the evening of the 26th.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you went and saw this patient; yes?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And then at some later time the police basically followed you home. What time did you go back home?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 8.15, 8.30, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it was very shortly after that then you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And was it uniformed Chetniks that arrested you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all Chetniks. It was the police wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How could you --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How could you tell they were Chetniks? How did you know they were Chetniks? Did they say they were Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They boasted that they were Chetniks. They didn't just say that. They boasted about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let me have you look now at Exhibit DB85, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I ask what -- can I ask what that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Ackerman, is this a short question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. This is going to go on for a long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I would suggest that we break now, because it's time for the break, and we resume immediately afterwards. We'll break for 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Gustin has a drawing for me, if I can get it. And what I want to do is put it on the ELMO and give the witness a marker. My system seems to have died, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For a moment it did. But now it's come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Oh, there we go. It's back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, you now have a nice clean inaccurate drawing of Manjaca in front of you. And what I'd like you to do is on the particular barn that was the one that you were in, just put a "1."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And on the gate that you say is the gate that's shown in Exhibit P810 -- and if you want to see it again, we'll show it to you so you can be certain -- but on the gate you say is that gate, just put a big "X" there.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And next to it write "810." And next to both of those marks, put your initials.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that would become DB86, Your Honour. And I'd offer it. And could the witness be given back P810 for just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir in this -- you told us earlier that what was going on in this photograph is you were waiting there for the guard to open the gate so that you could go to the infirmary where you worked; correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And so it's your testimony that the only way you could get from the barracks where you stayed - at least part of the time - to the infirmary where you worked was to go through this gate.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the guard doesn't seem to have a weapon. Did the guards not have weapons?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, there was this bench here where he would sit. And two or three of them would be there. The main guard was at the observation post. But during the day, there were no problems here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is he didn't have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How would he open the gate?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the photograph, it looks like there's a big brass padlock on the opposite side of the gate from where the guard is. Doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it. But the gate would be opened either from the inside or the outside. But I didn't pay attention to that. It wasn't important to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How many times did you go through that gate going back and forth to the infirmary?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5.000 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want you to now look at Exhibit DB85. Actually, you can't look at it but we'll put it on the ELMO. I need to -- since there's no B/C/S version of it, I'm just going to have the read parts of it to you and ask you to tell me if what is there is correct. First of all, I should tell you that this purports to be a news story, an article, written by a gentleman named Zoltan Nemeth. It's part 9 of a ten part series. It's dated 24 August 1992. It's apparently from a publication, although I'm not certain about this, called Novi Sad Madjari [phoen] FCO. But I don't know if that's the name of the publication. Apparently comes from Novi Sad and apparently is a Hungarian publication of some form. This person Zoltan Nemeth speaks about making a visit to Manjaca I suppose in late July, early August or sometime in August perhaps of 1992. Tell me if what he reports here is correct. He reports going into a stable. He says six rows of prisoners sit on the ground. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "There is a blanket under each of them. None of them wears shoes." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What part of that is not correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct to say that there was a blanket under all of them. And some people were wearing their shoes and others weren't. When they were lying down, everyone would take their shoes off. That was normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "They are not supposed to stand up except if so ordered." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "They are not permitted to walk around"; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "Every 20 minutes they allow 20 prisoners to go to the toilet and breathe fresh air"; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He says: "The people are skinny. Their faces and eyes are emaciated." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "They sit quietly because they are not permitted to converse." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "All of them have hair heads lowered. Only a very few raise their heads to look at us." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He then conducts an interview with a gentleman named Sead Ahmedagic. Did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know the name and the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He asks Sead, "How are they treating you here?" And he says that Sead responded: "Well, badly." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's true, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I better ask that differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is it true what Sead reportedly said that, he was treated badly there as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Still --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I mean, I'm afraid -- I know he was later on mentioned. How is he to know what this man said to the reporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's true. And I'm not really asking him if he knows what the man said to the reporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If the man said to the reporter that he was treated badly there, was he telling the reporter the truth?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he said so, yes, he was telling the truth. But I'm not in a position to say -- say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. If the man told the reporter in response to a question that the guards were beating the prisoners on occasion, was he telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If he told the reporter in answer to a question that they were making the prisoners work, was that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If he told the reporter in answer to a question regarding that work "We dig trenches. We load and unload things. We perform heavy physical work," would that have been true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "With regard to the food they received" --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Partially. Which part?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one dug trenches. Trenches weren't dug in Manjaca. There are no trenches in Manjaca, nowhere near Manjaca. And as far as physical work is concerned, yes, they would dig, plant potatoes, et cetera. They built things. Cut -- felled timber and so on. So it's partially true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "When asked about food," if the person replied that bad food and only a little of it, virtually nothing," would that have been true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When -- sorry. When? What date? When was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I believe the story was written on August 24th. It doesn't say what date this interview occurred. So I've given you all the information I can.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't answer you whether it was in June or early July, then yes. Later on, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you remember yourself speaking with this reporter Zoltan Nemeth from Novi Sad?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He says that he had a conversation with physician Enis Sabanovic. That would be you, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And he says that you were brought to the camp from Sanski Most. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And with regard to this issue about your arrest, he says that you told him that upon taking power, the Serbs made a public announcement asking anyone willing to aid in the situation to report to the police station, that you reported and were brought to Manjaca. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He says that even though you're a captive, you have it the best. You're allowed to leave the fenced-in camp, you can perform your work?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would we read the first sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Ms. Korner, please. Counsel, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm sorry. Could Mr. Ackerman kindly be kind enough to read the first sentence of that paragraph to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please do, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, all right. "He ceaselessly praises the commander and the soldiers. He praises them aloud so that everyone can hear him. I understand the poor fellow, even though a captive, he has it best. He's allowed to leave the fenced-in camp. He can perform his work and can even have confidence that they are going to have mercy on him."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are many statements there, Mr. Ackerman. I would suggest by take them one by one. It's definitely more fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Were you allowed to leave the fenced-in camp?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The fenced -- but the command. Everything was fenced. The command and all the rest was fenced. I didn't go out to work. It was always in the camp. I consider it the camp compound, both the compound and the infirmary. They allowed me to go to the command -- I mean, to leave the command where the stables were. I was allowed to go to the command where the infirmary was -- was. That, yes. But not to leave the camp. I never left the camp, never not for a single day. I never once went out of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He says you told him you were permitted to perform your work. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, allowed to perform my work. I was allowed to examine people, not perform my work -- well, yes. Yes, you could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And he says that you have -- you had confidence that they were going to have mercy on you. Did you tell him that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the next sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Mercy, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you tell him --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think if Ms. Korner wants to ask this witness questions on redirect about parts of this statement that I'm not reading, she's perfectly free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's misleading to the witness to only read selected parts when this document is being put to him. They should be put in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's correct, Ms. Korner. I suggest Mr. Ackerman, that if you are putting a paragraph or this alleged report paragraph by paragraph to the witness, please do so gradually one after the other. But try to be -- read the paragraph as complete as possible, please. Because otherwise, I mean, it's -- the last part of that sentence or of that paragraph is of course important. I mean, and the witness should be given the opportunity to answer or to comment about that last part of the paragraph as well. I mean, it's -- this is not exactly as I see it necessarily what the witness must have told the reporter if this encounter ever took place. But it's how the reporter is presenting his encounter with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There's a statement that -- and I've asked you this but I didn't get your answer. He says that you even have confidence that they're going to have mercy on you. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never mentioned any mercy. How can there be mercy at such a ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you have confidence that they are going to disregard the crime he has not even committed. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Crime? To forgive my crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He asks you whether the prisoners are beaten, and he says you answered no. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He says that you said with regard to beatings "There is no such thing here. The prisoners do not fight either." Did you say those things?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "On occasion a person is injured at work. That's all." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "Three-fourths of the cases involved, inflammation, laryngitis, bladder infection, kidney infection." Did you say that or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Impossible. When a man falls ill, he comes to me. But what you are saying about the journalists and -- where is this paper from? That is not correct. Oh, I have no comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm told that the translation was wrong. And let me ask you the question one more time, sir. "Three-fourths of the cases involved, inflammation, laryngitis, bladder infection, kidney infection." Is it correct that you said that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had to do with examination, if he asked me about the examination of patients, those who came to the infirmary, those who came out of the stables, most of them of course had colds. And a cold, yes, that would fit. But -- oh, no. I don't know. I don't understand this. You are listening to a journalist from Novi Sad. And if you are going by what he said, then it is all very nice and clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you said, "Serious cases --" he says you said, "Serious cases are taken to the Banja Luka hospital." Now, that is true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no severe -- serious cases, serious illnesses, except what I said in the beginning when we arrived, when a few -- some people were injured. But those were only a few cases. After that, nobody went to the hospital except the warrant officer whom I accompanied to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dr. Sabanovic, please answer these questions in relation to what you could have said or possibly never said to this journalist. In particular, if this meeting with this journalist ever took place. The questions are not related to whether there were serious cases, et cetera. Mr. Ackerman's question is related to what this journalist is alleging that you told him and on the basis of which he wrote this article or this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. That's not quite right. Mr. Ackerman actually this time was asking him -- he actually said to him, "Isn't it true that serious cases were taken to Banja Luka hospital?"

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. I asked him if he told -- or I meant to ask him at least, if that's what he told the journalist.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's not actually what you asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what you're -- you're to answer. I mean, the allegation here is that you had -- you were interviewed by this journalist. You said you don't recollect, remember having ever been interviewed by this journalist. And all the subsequent questions are based on the assumption that you were actually interviewed by this journalist. Is what he says that you told him here correct or not? Is it a faithful report of this interview or not? I mean, because your answer -- your first answer, you did not exclude that there was ever such an interview. You said you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The final statement here that I want to ask you about, sir, is this. The journalist claim that is you said this: "I believe that it is important to state that thus far not a single patient of ours has died." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except -- perhaps I said yesterday that we had only one patient die of natural causes. And I said it before this Chamber, before this Court. And I don't know even if I talked with this man. Do you know that it was ten years ago? Ten years have passed, and it's a little bit absurd for you to now talk about journalists in Manjaca interviewing somebody in Manjaca, the death camp, to say something opposite to -- or what I didn't -- to what didn't suit them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Oh, I understand that position, sir. And it really is difficult ten years down the road to remember all these things and to get them right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In your -- I don't think that answer got recorded. Yes, it is. Okay. Thank you. In your testimony yesterday, sir -- and I want to ask you just a question or two about Betonirka. In your testimony yesterday, pages 27 and 28 of the LiveNote, you're talking about Miladin Papic, who was a person you knew. You said that he -- you treated his family and that he was the commander of that facility apparently at Betonirka. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And according to the transcript, it says that once he saw you and the condition you were in, he resigned his position. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So he left his job as commander as soon as he saw what had happened to you; is that -- is that what you were explaining to the Trial Chamber yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You told the Trial Chamber that he never explained to you why you were being treated the way you were but that he helped you and without his help it was, you said -- these are your words "Otherwise I would have been killed 100 per cent." That's what you said; right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, how many people were there in Betonirka during that three days that you were there?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In garage -- there were up to 50 people in one of the garages. But there were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in all of the garages, do you have any idea the total number of people that were at Betonirka while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How many people were killed that you're aware of while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know of any? Do you know of one person that was killed at Betonirka while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is it your understanding that Miladin Papic was protecting everybody there?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You then went to Hasan Kikic, I believe it's called. It's the school, I think. And you were asked on page 30 by Ms. Korner: "The people who were guarding you there, were they ordinary policemen or military policemen?" And your answer is recorded as follows, sir: "There was a war. There are no ordinary policemen any more. There's a war on."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes? And then later at page 47 of the transcript, Ms. Korner was talking to you about the prisoners at Manjaca, and you were asked if any of them were really prisoners of war. And you answered at page 47: "There was no war. There was no war at all. There was no war." That appears three times in your answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry. Could you read on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was never --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I do think it's misleading to take selective quotes out like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I remember this --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'll read the whole answer if you want me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because he was referring to a particular --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "I can tell you quite sincerely and truthfully all those who came from Sanski Most, who from Kljuc. I don't know about others because I wasn't in touch with them. But the people from Sanski Most, there was no resistance in our town. There was no war."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, when you talked about the policeman at Hasan Kikic, that was Sanski Most. And your answer to the question there was: "There was a war. There are no ordinary policemen any more. There was a war on." I'll read your answer later on page 47 again. "There was no resistance in our town. There was no war. There wasn't a shot fired when we were captured in our homes or at our working places. So there was no war there at all."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "There was no resistance."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain? May I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm not finished, sir. I'm not finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the translation, Your Honour. If I read any faster, they'll stop me. I told you I'd read the entire answer, and now I'm doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, Mr. Ackerman. And before the witness answers, I'll make something clear to him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "I loved when the CNN would come and other international broadcasters, and they would say 'this one was captured on the front' I can't understand, this and I deny it. I cannot talk about it at all, not a single one. I am very familiar with the municipality of Sanski Most. Not a single person, not a single detainee from Sanski Most at Manjaca was a prisoner of war. There was no war. There was no resistance. A couple of policemen would simply bring 50 people from a particular village. What kind? What resistance? What front line? What war are we talking about?" Now, that was your answer a few pages after you talked about there being a war in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, pay attention to me, Dr. Sabanovic, please. Because the question is clear enough. But it took sometime, because it involved -- to unfold because it involved also reading excerpts from your testimony of yesterday. The question that is being put to you is a very simple one. There are two moments during your testimony yesterday. At one moment you're saying policemen, not policemen -- there was a war. There were no policemen at the time of war. There is no question of a policeman. And then the next moment you're saying that there was no war and you're trying to explain that anyone talking of the existence of a war doesn't know what he's talking about. So what you're being asked to do is to explain to this Chamber whether you were contradicting yourself yesterday or whether there is an explanation for what you testified yesterday in these two different moments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First I was surprised. Now, it is not a contradiction. When there is a war, you have two sides fighting against each other. In this case, there was no resistance from the Muslim Catholic side in Sanski Most. Nobody had a rifle, nor was a bullet fired. But the Serb side came, pillaged, killed, fired. The Chetnik side, the Serb side. And that is why I said that there was no war. I apologise. I raised my voice. And that is that we offered no resistance. But we were taken to camps, civilians were taken to camps, because it now turns out that I was on the front line in the war and that I'm a prisoner of war. And I'm a civilian victim, because I was taken from home and that is why I said that there was no war. But war needs two sides fighting, and then you have a war. But to round up civilians and drive them all to concentration camps, that is not a war. That is a genocide, killing, annihilation of one nation of a people. That is two peoples.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I totally understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My question now is: Why then when you were asked earlier by Ms. Korner about the policemen that were guarding you, whether they were ordinary policemen or not, you told her "There was a war. There are no ordinary policemen any more. There's a war on"? So if you say there was no war, why did you give her that answer?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave it because it was called war. But there was no resistance in Banja Luka. In Sanski Most, in Prijedor, there was no resistance. People were killed, intellectuals and peasants and others, and that is -- well, it depends how you look at it. There are two sides. There is one side which is superior, which is armed, which is destroying, and there is the other side which is unarmed and which perishes. When seven doctors in a town are killed, then there is nothing else, a genocide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's enough. Mr. Ackerman, you can move to the next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: At page 36 of the transcript, sir, you were asked by Ms. Korner: "Would you accept that it was on or about the 6th of June of 1992 that you went to Manjaca?" Your answer -- and I'll read the whole answer, sir: "Why, yes. Of course I didn't know the date when I left. There was no way I could note the dates. So as of the WC onward, I simply don't know anything about that. I didn't have anything, nor nobody explained it. Nobody mentioned it. Nobody cared what date it was. But yes, it must have been there give or take." Now, in the statement that you gave to the German investigators, you told them that you went to Manjaca -- you told them -- it's on the second page of the German statement -- that you were in Manjaca from 3 June to 24 November. And you were then -- you were then challenged about that, I think is a way to describe it. Another witness who allegedly arrived at the Manjaca camp with you said that he was taken there on 6 June 1992. What do you say to this?" Your answer, according to --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say yes. I don't care whether it was the 3rd or the 6th. I didn't keep up with the dates. I still don't know them. Don't ask me about dates; ask me about months. Only about months, or two months. Come on. It was a horror.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: According to the German authorities, you said whether or not it was correct about June 3rd. You said: "My answer is correct. I am sure of it."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't care.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "I came on 3 June 1992." "My answer is correct. I'm sure of it. I came to Manjaca camp on 3 June 1992." Now, are you sure of it or not?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that a couple of days mean nothing to me, and I told everybody, "Don't ask me about dates," because I wasn't getting ready for my baccalaureate, for my matriculation.
