But for -- but to survive in something that did not exist in Europe, even in World War II. Could have been the 6th. Whatever way you take it, I couldn't care less. I don't deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You know, if that's the case, why didn't you say to these people who were asking you questions in Germany, "I don't know whether it was the 3rd or the 6th. It could have been the 5th or the 7th. Don't ask me about dates." Why didn't you say that to them?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not think these are mistakes. I do not think it is important, and I paid no attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My question is: Why didn't you say to them that it was not important, that you didn't care what date it was and they shouldn't ask you about dates? Why didn't you say that to them?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that to everybody. From the beginning I was saying that. There are still these formalities which are surprising. To look where the stables were or what had I known that it would be like, this perhaps I would have drawn a picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you think this is funny what we're doing here? Are you enjoying this and smiling at me like that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of it. Not all of it. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, please. I call you to order. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Instead of telling these German authorities that the date was not important to you, what you said to them was, "My answer is correct. I am sure of it. I came to Manjaca camp on 3 June 1992." Now, do you want to deny that's what you told them? You go ahead. You can deny that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This has already been -- I'm now going to do the American thing. This has been asked and answered. And Your Honour has already told Mr. Ackerman --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Objection sustained. Let's proceed, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There's a matter that I'm somewhat confused about and I need you to straighten out for me. At page 37 and 38 of the transcript, you were talking about getting on the trucks that took you to Manjaca. And you talked about people's hands being tied two by two. Were your hands tied, or was this other people on the trucks?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, a few moments ago I was reading to you from the report of that reporter from Novi Sad. And I asked you when people were seriously injured they'd be sent to Banja Luka by ambulance, and you said no, that's not the case. I believe that was your response. And if I'm wrong about that, you tell me I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not wrong. But if I might say, it was seldom. It just did not take place. I said in my statement that it comes as a surprise how resilient people are considering the state they are in. And they did not die of natural causes, nor were there any serious illnesses. There were no infectious diseases, no epidemics broke out, and that's what I said. That it came as a surprise. Certain things I have tremendous life experience. But there are certain things, certain dubious things which I cannot accept. Of course a doctor will send a serious case to where such a case belongs to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you tell us at one point that you were kicked by someone and flew through the air for 2 or 3 centimetres -- 2 or 3 - not centimetres - 2 or 3 metres?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You actually flew through the air for 2 or 3 metres as a result of a kick.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. In the stomach. A policeman about 2 metres tall hit me. I flew over others who were beneath me about 2 or 3 metres. That's clear. I didn't even weigh 50 kilos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday you talked about being asked to examine four young men who had a skin disease which you diagnosed as scabies and how the policemen brought four bottles of medicine that you used to treat them with. And then in the middle of that answer or halfway through that answer you also started to talk about a young man who had a broken left shoulder and a cast that went up to his elbow and the cast did not assist his broken shoulder but made it worse. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And this all occurred rather early, shortly after your arrival at Manjaca, because these four young men were building that fence we've been talking about; right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: At page 56, you told us that you examined this young man with the cast.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "After I examined him" -- you said this: "After I examined him, he was sent to Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And then there appears this sentence: "And I must add, I left immediately." Surely you didn't leave right after that, did you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, it -- the implication one gets is that you left the camp right after you examined this man and he was sent to Banja Luka. That's not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not logical. If you weren't listening, that's something else. On the first day of the arrival in the camp, it was dusk -- if I went anywhere, I went to the stables. I couldn't have gone to Banja Luka or up into the sky or anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dr. Sabanovic, one moment. Mr. Ackerman is reading out what the interpreters and the other officers put down for us as having been stated by you yesterday. If it's not clear, if it doesn't make sense to you, you're not allowed to attack Mr. Ackerman. You're just, please, clarify things to us. This is what we have. What we have here says that after you sent this person to Banja Luka, you left immediately. Did you leave? And if it has been reported like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the stables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, to the stables. Okay. So that's -- that's the explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman by the name of Alexandar Bijelic nicknamed Aco? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is that the person you were talking about maybe out there with the trucks when the large number of people were shipped in from Prijedor? The person you were talking about earlier today?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. No. No. That's not the person. That person, his name was -- his last name was Stojnic. He was demobilised in Banja Luka. He would come to my house. He contacted me, and I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What do you know about Aco Bijelic?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a nurse. He studied medicine for two years. Later on he became a nurse. He worked in the military hospital. And he came in an official capacity to Manjaca. He replaced a nurse in Manjaca and he worked there together with me. He was in the infirmary and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So he worked with you in the infirmary at Manjaca as a nurse.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: On page 72 of the LiveNote transcript, you talked about a young man who stepped on a mine and his right leg was cut off below the knee. And you told us that an ambulance came and took him off to Banja Luka to the surgery ward. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Dr. Derviskadic, you told us at page 58 of your testimony yesterday that he did not want to testify. I think you said "That is what he told me." When did you talk to Dr. Derviskadic about --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When did you talk to him about coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from other people. He had taken Swiss nationality and he said he wouldn't come to testify before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Let me read you answer, because it's a little bit ambiguous. And I'd just ask you to explain it to me. You were asked about him, and you said: "Yes. His name is Meho Derviskadic, who now lives in Switzerland."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "He did not want to testify because --" there's a pause "-- well, I don't know. He was admitted into Swiss nationality and so on and so forth. That is what he told me." What did --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I heard. I didn't speak to him. That's something I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So what you said was not true or it was -- it was taken down wrong? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true. It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say it's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not important.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to ask you about Emir Mulalic, who is a person you say died in Manjaca. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You said that his sternum was broken when you saw him, he was bleeding at the mouth and at the nose, and that "We established that he was dead." Right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In your statement to the German authorities - and I'm at page 13 of the English version - you were asked about Emir Mulalic, and you'd said that you were certain that the dead man was Emir Mulalic, "whom I had known previously." And then further down the page, apparently Dr. Derviskadic had made a statement - although it's not totally clear - that you had reanimated Emir Mulalic. And you said: "I can state that I am certain that I did not reanimate Emir Mulalic. He'd been my patient before the war." That happened during those conversations you had with the German authorities, didn't it, that interchange we just talked about?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want you to look now at a -- at an exhibit in this case. It's a Prosecutor's exhibit, P754.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, we have three minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, we'd better stop. We're not going to get there. We'll start with this in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just inquire. We've got two witnesses lined up for tomorrow. I don't know how much longer the Defence would like to be with this witness. Any idea, anybody?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Looks like I have an hour left; maybe a little less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll probably finish tomorrow, perhaps before the second break -- I'll certainly finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Dr. Sabanovic, we are not finished with you as yet. You will have to return tomorrow. But I'm pretty sure that we will finish with you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are adjourned until tomorrow afternoon at 2.15. No. Tomorrow it will be in Courtroom number III, and the same applies for the day after tomorrow. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The reason is Milosevic is sitting till 4.00 in the afternoon. So we'll have to vacate this room because of the Albanians. Thank you.
